setup: The web store is available through a browser and is presented as an online shopping site intended for first-time online shoppers and new online business owners.
action: A new visitor opens the site's home page and reviews the available shopping and store-management areas.
expected_observation: The site is recognizable as a web store with customer shopping features and business management access paths suitable for inexperienced online commerce users and new store owners.

setup: A store owner is signed in with business-management access to the GAMMA-J Web Store.
action: The store owner opens the management area to review products, customer records, and order activity.
expected_observation: The system provides store-management functions that allow the owner to manage the online retail business, including access to product and customer administration.

setup: A sales personnel user is signed in with staff privileges.
action: The staff member opens the catalog and customer administration areas to perform daily retail maintenance tasks.
expected_observation: The system grants the sales personnel access to product and customer account management functions appropriate for retail operations.

setup: A customer accesses the web store from a browser without needing staff credentials.
action: The customer browses the product catalog, adds an item to the cart, and proceeds to place an order.
expected_observation: The system supports customer shopping activities, including browsing products, maintaining a cart, and submitting orders.

setup: A staff member is signed in and is viewing the product administration screen with permission to manage catalog items.
action: The staff member creates a new product with a name, price, and category, then updates the product's details and saves the changes.
expected_observation: The new product appears in the catalog and the updated product information is stored and shown accurately after saving.

setup: A staff member is signed in and is viewing an existing customer account in the customer management area.
action: The staff member creates a new customer account and then edits the customer's contact details or account status before saving.
expected_observation: The customer account is created successfully and the updated account information is retained and displayed correctly.

setup: The store catalog contains multiple available products and a customer is viewing the storefront.
action: The customer opens the product listing page without applying any search or filter criteria.
expected_observation: The system displays the available products in the catalog for browsing.

setup: The catalog contains products with distinct names and a customer is on the product search page.
action: The customer enters a product name in the search field and submits the search.
expected_observation: The system returns products whose names match the entered search term and presents the matching results to the customer.

setup: The catalog contains products across multiple categories and price points, and the customer is viewing the product listing page.
action: The customer selects a category filter and sets a minimum and maximum price range, then applies the filters.
expected_observation: The product list is narrowed to items in the chosen category and within the selected price range.

setup: A customer is viewing a product detail page for an available item and the shopping cart is accessible.
action: The customer clicks Add to Cart for the selected product.
expected_observation: The product is added to the shopping cart and the cart reflects the added item.

setup: A customer has an item in the shopping cart with an initial quantity already displayed.
action: The customer changes the item quantity to a different valid number and saves or updates the cart.
expected_observation: The cart updates to show the new quantity for that item and the cart contents reflect the change.

setup: A customer has one or more products in the shopping cart.
action: The customer removes one item from the cart.
expected_observation: The selected item is removed from the cart and no longer appears in the cart contents.

setup: A customer has items in the shopping cart and is viewing the cart summary page.
action: The customer reviews the cart before proceeding to checkout.
expected_observation: The system shows the cart total, including the summed cost of the items currently in the cart, before checkout is started.

setup: A customer has items in the cart and has opened the checkout flow.
action: The customer enters the required order details, confirms the items in the order, and submits the order.
expected_observation: The order is accepted and the submitted order details and item confirmation are recorded as a placed order.

setup: A customer has successfully submitted an order through checkout.
action: The order submission completes.
expected_observation: An immediate order confirmation is displayed to the customer, showing that the order was placed successfully.

setup: A staff member is signed in to the GAMMA-J Web Store admin area, and a customer has just submitted a new order successfully.
action: The staff member opens the order dashboard or notification area.
expected_observation: A new order alert or visible order entry appears showing that a new customer order has been placed, including the order reference and time of submission.

setup: A customer is signed in to their account and has at least one completed or previously placed order in the system.
action: The customer opens the order history page from their account menu.
expected_observation: The system displays a list of the customer's past orders with relevant order details such as order date, order number, and order status.

setup: A staff member is signed in to the admin area, and the store has recorded sales transactions over a selected reporting period.
action: The staff member opens the sales report view and selects a date range.
expected_observation: The system displays basic sales reporting for the chosen period, such as total orders, total sales value, and sales activity summary.

setup: A customer is signed in to their account and their profile currently contains saved contact details and a delivery address.
action: The customer opens their account profile, edits their contact details and delivery address, and saves the changes.
expected_observation: The updated contact details and address are stored successfully and are shown on the account profile page after saving.

setup: A first-time customer is shopping in the web store and has items in the cart, with no existing customer profile or saved checkout details.
action: The customer proceeds to checkout and completes the simple checkout flow using only the required purchase and delivery information.
expected_observation: The checkout process accepts the first-time customer and allows the order to be placed without requiring a prior account or advanced setup steps.

setup: A customer is on the checkout page with one or more items in the cart and attempts to submit the order.
action: The customer leaves the name, contact email, or delivery address blank and clicks the place order button.
expected_observation: The system blocks order submission and displays validation messages indicating that the customer's name, contact email, and delivery address are required.

setup: A customer is on the checkout page with items ready to purchase.
action: The customer leaves the contact number field empty and completes the rest of the required checkout information before submitting the order.
expected_observation: The order is accepted successfully, and the absence of a contact number does not prevent submission.

setup: The product catalog contains one or more active products available for browsing.
action: A customer opens the product listing or product details page.
expected_observation: Each displayed product shows its product name, short description, price, and current availability status.

setup: A product in the catalog has an image attached to its product record.
action: A customer opens the product listing or product details page for that product.
expected_observation: The product image is displayed alongside the product information.

setup: A customer has completed checkout successfully and the order has been accepted by the system.
action: The customer submits the final purchase from the checkout confirmation step.
expected_observation: An immediate success confirmation is displayed, clearly indicating that the purchase was successful and providing a confirmation reference or order acknowledgement.

setup: The first release scope for GAMMA-J Web Store is being reviewed by a staff member or product owner.
action: They inspect the available features and navigation in the release candidate.
expected_observation: The system supports the prioritized core functions of order placement, shopping cart, product browsing, and product management, and these core areas are readily accessible in the product.

setup: A release candidate is available for review before launch.
action: A staff member explores the storefront and admin capabilities to check the breadth of included functions.
expected_observation: The first release remains centered on core buying and management tasks, with no excessive extra features crowding the main user flows.

setup: A new store user with little e-commerce experience opens the GAMMA-J Web Store for the first time.
action: The user tries to browse products, add an item to the cart, and proceed through checkout without assistance.
expected_observation: The interface is understandable and the main shopping steps can be completed without training or needing specialist guidance.

setup: A new store owner is preparing to launch the shop and has access to the admin setup area.
action: The owner configures basic store settings, adds a product, and publishes the shop using the available guided options.
expected_observation: The store can be brought into service through straightforward admin actions without requiring significant technical help.

setup: The web store is available for normal use by customers and staff.
action: Users browse products, place orders, and manage store data during routine use over time.
expected_observation: The system operates reliably, with the main screens remaining easy to learn and without frequent failures during normal use.

setup: An order has been successfully placed in the GAMMA-J Web Store and the system is ready to send an order confirmation notification to the customer.
action: The notification delivery step is triggered for the completed order.
expected_observation: The acceptance outcome is treated as unresolved: the system requirement does not yet define whether the customer receives an advanced confirmation notification or a simple confirmation notification, so this behavior remains unverified until a product decision is recorded.
